messages.content: 你能給我標準差為10、樣本大小為50、樣本平均值為25的平均值95%信賴區間嗎？同樣的，你能為樣本大小為150的情況做同樣的事嗎？

function.name: confidence_interval_calculate
function.description: Calculate the confidence interval for a mean. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample.

confidence_level.description: The level of confidence. Default is 0.9. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Can you give me the 95% confidence interval for the mean with standard deviation=10, sample size=50, sample mean=25? Also do same for sample size=150." We need to compute using t-distribution or normal approximation? For CI calculation we can use z if population SD known; but they gave sample std dev as 10 (maybe estimate). Usually use t distribution when sigma unknown and n small (<30) else approximate normal. But here n=50 >30 so could use normal approx. However typical formula uses s/sqrt(n)*t_{alpha/2,n-1}. We'll assume t.

We have to call tool `confidence_interval_calculate` which expects arguments: sample_std_dev, sample_size, sample_mean, optional confidence_level default .9. They want 95%, so set confidence_level=0.95.

We'll produce two calls:

First: sample_std_dev=10, sample_size=50, sample_mean=25, confidence_level=0.95.

Second: sample_std_dev=10, sample_size=150, sample_mean=25, confidence_level=0.95.

But note: In the prompt, the tool's signature says confidence_level defaults to 0.9. So we pass 0.95 explicitly.

Thus output should include results from both calls. Use separate JSON objects per call. Probably each result will contain lower bound and upper bound. Let's format accordingly.
